# PLAN — iteration 3
## Current state assessment
The verified incumbent is timing-feasible at 7 LUTs and 9 FFs, so this iteration must strictly reduce LUTs (or match LUTs and reduce FFs) to improve the objective. Iterations 1 and 2 both used an 8-bit counter but tried different wrap logic; both passed behavior and timing yet increased LUTs to 10. The current top’s numeric latency is unknown, so no numeric annotation is required; preserve its registered PWM output and reset behavior.

## Hypothesis
Splitting the modulo-256 counter into two 4-bit incrementing sections may reduce LUT use by limiting carry logic to each nibble while preserving the same counter sequence and PWM output.

## Instruction for generator
Replace the 32-bit counter with an 8-bit phase counter divided into low and high nibbles: increment the low nibble every active cycle and increment the high nibble only when the old low nibble is `4'hf`, allowing natural modulo-256 wrap. Keep the synchronous reset to zero and the registered output assignment equivalent to `counter < duty` using the pre-edge phase value. Do not add latency or a numeric `@latency` annotation; retain the candidate only if the unchanged simulation, routed timing, and metric integrity gates pass and the LUT/FF objective strictly improves over the verified incumbent.
